sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Social Commerce via Short Video Platforms

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch common law, English-law-inspired company and commercial statutes, African customary law, and constitutional supremacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment
Agreement on the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
Convention between South Africa and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation
United States-South Africa Income Tax Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022), read with Companies Regulations, 2011; Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) and Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Control Regulations; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; CIPC Beneficial Ownership filing requirements under the Companies Act; FIC Guidance Notes 6, 7 and 9.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each non-resident beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Recognized notary public in the document-issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization at a South African embassy/high commission if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles of association, register of directors and current certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry / registrar of companies in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds / proof-of-funds statement for the initial shareholder contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign licensed bank or financial institution where the funding account is held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization (depending on bank account jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police/criminal good conduct certificate for each non-resident director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police, criminal record bureau or ministry of interior of each person's country of ordinary residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening before incorporation and at onboarding against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (iii) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists; (iv) FIC section 26A freezing and prohibition notices issued under FICA; (v) domestic targeted financial sanctions lists adopted under POCDATARA. PEP controls: obliged institutions must apply enhanced due diligence to South African and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members and close associates; must establish source of wealth and source of funds; ongoing transactional monitoring after incorporation. The FIC expects accountable institutions to verify each UBO and director and retain all documentary evidence for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za / www.cipc.co.za) – name reservation module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be composed of letters of the Latin alphabet, Arabic numerals or a combination, and may be in any of South Africa's official languages. If a foreign trade name is in non-Latin script, a Latin-script transliteration must be submitted and shown on the notice of incorporation. The name must not be confusing, offensive, falsely imply government/royal/sponsorship, or resemble an existing registered name/protected mark under section 11 of the Companies Act, as construed in common-law passing-off and trademark principles.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended at CIPC's discretion, upon a written request and payment of the prescribed extension fee, for one additional period of up to six months before expiry. If CIPC rejects a name on grounds of undesirability, confusion or a prohibited token, the applicant may, within 20 business days of the rejection notice, submit a 'name reconsideration' application through the CIPC e-Services portal with revised wording, supporting consents from the concerned regulator, a trademark availability opinion, or a professional explanation of why the name is not undesirable. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act within 30 business days of the CIPC decision, using the prescribed Companies Tribunal application form, together with the CIPC rejection notice and a memorandum; alternatively, the applicant may simply file a new, clean name reservation and proceed with the registration step.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office with a physical street address in South Africa is mandatory for service of process; a PO Box is not acceptable. A serviced/virtual office that provides a physical South African address, mail handling, and a responsible local agent is generally permissible for a private e-commerce company, provided the address is not a mere virtual mailbox without a local presence. For a TikTok Shop retail seller, home-based offices, co-working spaces and registered-agent offices are acceptable as commercial substance unless the acquiring bank or payment processor insists on a distinct business address for merchant KYC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% to 15% annual likelihood for a single-member private company in low-risk e-commerce: no mandatory unannounced CIPC/FIC inspection for non-regulated retailers, but a suspicious transaction report, high-risk PEP nexus, or inconsistent UBO filings can trigger FIC inspection or SARS/Auditor verification within 30 days; merchant banks also conduct documentary premises verification, not necessarily physical, on onboarding.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CIPC published tariff schedule (ZAR equivalent, USD at prevailing central-bank rate)

CIPC beneficial ownership (BO) notification filing for all identified UBOs and directors

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CIPC electronic filing tariff (if any) and required statutory submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of 3–5 hours at senior corporate attorney hourly rate of USD 180–230

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / business address service for one year (physical address and legal service handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered company secretary, business address provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market charge for serviced registered office (ZAR 8,000–9,500 equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance consultant or legal practitioner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed fee for KYC pack and FIC-compliant due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille/consular legalization and preparation of the mandatory foreign-document bundle (passports, corporate extracts, bank references, police certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country notary, competent apostille authority and South African mission if consular legalization required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Scale of notary/consular fees; average estimate for four documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English translation of non-English corporate, passport and proof-of-funds documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: South African accredited translator or sworn translator

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Global SARS tax practitioner professional fee; SARS itself charges no registration fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: South African business bank account and payment-rail facilitation (bank FICA onboarding, Wise Business verification, TikTok Shop seller KYC preparation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SADC commercial bank / Wise B2B / TikTok Shop merchant on-boarding compliance team and law firm facilitator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market fee for corporate bank onboarding and merchant account compliance pack

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (sections 13–19, 32 and 66) read with the Companies Regulations 2011; Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 for post-incorporation tax registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A), Initial Directors' Consent (Form CoR 14.1B) and Registered Office Consent (Form CoR 14.1C)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Shares may be issued without escrow deposit; the board must certify solvency and liquidity under section 4 of the Act. Authorised share capital may be denominated in any currency under the MOI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company be incorporated under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and that the executive officer is authorised to file with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1), the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A), and the Initial Directors' Consent (Form CoR 14.1B); FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be a physical address in the Republic of South Africa subject to municipal zoning approval; FURTHER RESOLVED that the inaugural directors are appointed, being authorised to open corporate bank accounts, appoint an external auditor where section 84 so requires, procure SARS income tax and VAT registrations, and obtain all municipal trading licences for internet and social commerce retail; ALL RESOLUTIONS effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to four proposed company names via the CIPC e-Services website. The CIPC system will screen the names against existing registrations and active trademarks; upon approval the name is reserved for six months. The reservation receipt is attached to the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Certified proof of identity of each incorporator/director
Consent to act as director (preliminary, if available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the name is refused, file an amended name reservation with revised names; alternatively incorporate under an enterprise number and apply for a name change post-registration under section 24 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and Attesting Notary (optional); lodged with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI in accordance with Schedule 1 of the Companies Act and prescribe the company's authorised share capital, incorporation date, pre-emptive rights, quorum rules and any special limitations for a private (Pty) company. Every incorporator must sign the MOI, with signatures witnessed; the signed MOI is then uploaded for electronic filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a technical query on MOI clauses, file a revised MOI with the requested amendments and submit an explanatory letter within 20 business days; if rejected, resubmit through CIPC 'Resubmission' workflow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Notice of Incorporation and Initial Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form CoR 14.1 together with the MOI (CoR 14.1A), Initial Directors' Consent (CoR 14.1B) and Registered Office Consent (CoR 14.1C). Pay the statutory registration fee electronically. CIPC will scrutinise the filing and issue a Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3) with an enterprise number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended, correct the reason code indicated on the CIPC transaction report and resubmit; for name or consent issues, file a rectification notice under section 24 and Companies Act Regulation 16.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Income Tax and VAT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon CIPC incorporation, SARS will allocate an automatic income tax reference number. File a VAT 101 application where projected taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million per annum; register for PAYE and UIF if employees are engaged. Submit bank account confirmation and director details to complete the SARS eFiling profile.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the income tax number is not generated automatically, submit a Notice of Objection via SARS eFiling or contact the SARS Registration Contact Centre to enforce the registration timeline; apply for a Tax Compliance Status once filings are up to date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compensation Fund (COIDA) and Unemployment Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (Compensation Fund and UIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer; submit the Employer Registration form to the Compensation Commissioner to obtain a COIDA letter of good standing, and activate the UIF employer account through the Department of Employment and Labour or SARS eFiling. Maintain annual return of earnings filings thereafter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Compensation Fund queries the risk class or payroll data, file a correction request with supporting payslips; if registration is delayed, escalate to the Provincial office of the Department of Employment and Labour.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Trading Licence and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality Business Licensing and Economic Development Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business registration or trading licence covering the physical e-commerce fulfilment premises. Submit zoning certificates, fire safety clearance, electrical certificate of compliance, and a copy of the lease or title deed to establish lawful use of the premises for retail storage and dispatch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses or conditions the licence, apply to the municipal manager for reconsideration and independently appeal to the MEC within 90 days under section 5 of the Business Act 71 of 1991; cure municipal compliance deficiencies and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Municipal Business Licensing Authority (e.g., City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality Licensing and Economic Development Department) — no separate national sector licence applies to ISIC 4791 internet retail
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Registration/Trading Certificate for General Retail and E-Commerce Fulfilment (ISIC 4791)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and Local Municipal Environmental Health Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category C) only if the premises exceed thresholds in Listing Notices 1–3 (GN 983/2014); ordinary retail store/warehouse operations are generally exempt from a full EIA
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with municipal trade effluent by-laws (pH 6–9, suspended solids and COD limits); no Atmospheric Emission Licence is required absent listed activities under NEM:AQA; packaging and general waste must be disposed in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under the Fire Brigade Services Act 99 of 1987; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance, including structural load inspection, electrical certificate of compliance, emergency evacuation plan and workplace risk assessment for the e-commerce fulfilment unit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); administrative and filing portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); customs clearance executed through the SACU/SARS customs operating system (EAAS/CDS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Upon incorporation through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), the (Pty) Ltd is automatically registered as a taxpayer and SARS issues an Income Tax Reference Number; (2) within 14 days of incorporation, appoint a resident public officer as required by Section 99 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; (3) submit a VAT 101 application via eFiling or a SARS branch when taxable supplies exceed the compulsory R1,000,000 threshold, or elect voluntary registration from R50,000; (4) if employees are engaged, register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Skills Development Levy (SDL), and UIF; (5) non-resident shareholders must obtain a South African non-resident taxpayer reference number for dividend tax purposes and appoint a registered tax practitioner for local compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the (Pty) Ltd is a separate legal person taxed under the Income Tax Act at the 27% corporate rate (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023); no check-the-box pass-through election is available; profits distributed to shareholders are subject to 20% dividends tax; the social commerce retail activities are within the full territorial scope of South African taxation (worldwide income for resident companies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in South Africa. Relevant elections available: (a) VAT Act section 15 voluntary VAT registration election between R50,000 and R1,000,000 turnover; (b) Income Tax Act section 11D research and development allowance approval; (c) section 12B/12BA renewable energy allowances; (d) group relief elections under section 41 onwards for intra-group loss surrender; (e) statutory hybrid mismatch rules under sections 20A-20D apply compulsorily and cannot be elected out; (f) domestic reverse charge applies to certain imported services under section 7(1)(c) of the VAT Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R 1,000,000 in the preceding 12 months (compulsory turnover threshold); voluntary registration from R 50,000
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance and continuous transaction controls are not yet fully mandated; however, full tax invoices must be issued under section 20 of the VAT Act within 21 days of the supply, and the VAT 201 return is filed electronically via the SARS eFiling API; South Africa is phasing in OECD-style enhanced digital reporting under the SARS Modernisation roadmap (2025-2027); cross-border retail consignments are cleared in real time through the SACU/SARS Electronic Automated Assessment system utilising the SAD500 declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the TikTok Shop retailer supplies goods to non-residents and the goods are physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of the time of supply; under section 11(2), cross-border services (including offshore advertising, platform intermediation, and international logistics) are zero-rated where supplied to non-residents; the retailer must obtain and retain the export documentary evidence prescribed by section 54(5) of the VAT Act; failure to effect physical export reclassifies the supply as taxable at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) with SARS/SACU electronic clearance
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Courier Waybill evidencing physical movement to the foreign consignee
Commercial invoice referencing the VAT registration number and the zero-rating ground
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank statement proving foreign currency receipt from the non-resident buyer
Proof of delivery or acceptance at the port of export (customs clearance advice)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export zero-rating claims strictly under section 54(5); where documentation is deficient, the zero-rating is reversed and output VAT is assessed retrospectively with interest at the prescribed rate (repurchase rate plus 1%) compounded daily; the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 imposes understatement penalties ranging from 25% to 150% based on conduct (substantial understatement to intentional tax evasion); fraudulent export zero-rating exposes the entity and its public officer to criminal prosecution under sections 233-234 of the VAT Act (fine and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years); an additional tax clawback of up to 200% may be imposed under section 60(2); repeated non-compliance may trigger accelerated VAT filing, security deposits, or cancellation of VAT registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) of the National Treasury, with delegated authority to Authorised Dealers (commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, interest, dividends, and royalties, subject to standard documentary verification. Capital account transactions, including non-resident equity investment and cross-border loans, are permissible under the Exchange Control Regulations but must be routed through an authorised dealer, and reporting obligations under FinSurv Circulars apply. Profit remittance by a proprietary limited company is allowed for distributable profits provided the company satisfies the Companies Act solvency and liquidity test, the source of funds is clearly supported by audited financial statements, and the remittance is declared on the required FinSurv forms. No quantitative restriction on profit repatriation currently exists for bona fide non-resident shareholdings, but practical hurdles include proving inward capital status, obtaining a tax clearance certificate for large distributions, and completing FICA AML/KYC documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received through an authorised dealer in South Africa within 180 days of the date of shipment or, for certain e-commerce models, within 180 days of the completion of the sale and dispatch. The exporter must declare all export transactions on the required Exchange Control form via the authorised dealer, which is reconciled against the South African Revenue Service (SARS) customs export declaration, and the foreign currency must be surrendered to the authorised dealer unless a foreign-currency account retention licence was issued by FinSurv. There is no fixed statutory percentage of compulsory conversion to ZAR beyond the obligation to repatriate the full invoice value through a SARB-compliant channel; approved foreign-currency accounts allow holding of export proceeds for allowed periods, but any extension or deviation requires FinSurv approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Rand Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (FNB) – First National Bank of Southern Africa
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account and Global Money Multi-Currency Account
Capital Import Account and Transactional Business Account
Business Current Account and Forex Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a substitute for regulated banking, but High as a supplementary corridor. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and TikTok settlement partners cannot provide SARB-authorised dealer functions, local ZAR clearing, or statutory export-proceeds surrender processing. They may be used for USD/EUR/CNY pre-funded receipts and to optimise cross-border payment fees, but a South African licensed bank remains mandatory for capital injection, profit remittance, and tax reporting. The EMI must be onboarded as a foreign supplier and every flow in and out of the platform must be traceable through the authorised dealer reconciliation system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA requires account-taking institutions to verify the identity of all beneficial owners and directors to a reasonable standard. South African tier-1 banks generally require at least one director or a formally appointed company representative to attend an onboarding interview in person, although a growing number of banks accept hybrid remote onboarding with notarised/apostilled corporate documents, biometric identity verification, and independent third-party verification for low-to-moderate risk retail companies. For the TikTok Shop retail scope, physical attendance is recommended for the initial capital escrow account activation; fully remote onboarding is possible but will trigger a longer compliance review and a materially higher document chain burden.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ownership transparency for a proprietary limited company with non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholder register, sealed board resolution confirming the full shareholding structure, proof of source of funds (bank statements from the settling financial institution, signed share subscription agreement, and sworn affidavit or court-stamped declaration), and CIP documentation for each natural-person UBO above 25% including passport, proof of residential address, tax identification number, and clean public-source background check.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce payout inflows originating from TikTok Shop settlement entity and connected global payment aggregators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform seller agreement, distribution/escrow service schedules, TikTok Seller Centre statement extracts showing payout composition, invoice durability reports, transaction monitoring retention policy, and a formal merchant AML/CTF policy with commercial-payer due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire funding for share capital subscription in the capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes recording the investment, completed Form A / inward capital declaration as prescribed by the authorised dealer, single source-of-wealth statement, bank-to-bank MT103 with sender's declared origin, and signed undertaking by the non-resident subscriber to comply with exchange-control reporting timelines through the authorised dealer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement between the trading/inventory account and offshore supplier payments creating suspicion of trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full purchase orders, supplier VAT/tax invoices, customs export declarations, logistics transport documents, warehouse inbound/outbound ledger, and an item-level reconciliation trail connecting TikTok Shop payout statements to inventory purchase orders.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must subscribe shares via an incoming SWIFT MT103 or equivalent wire to a dedicated foreign-facilitated capital account at the authorised dealer. The remittance must reference the share-subscription agreement, use the designated balance-of-payments purpose code for 'Equity capital inflow from non-resident', and be accompanied by the correct inward declaring form required by the specific bank. The authorised dealer will verify the source of funds, register the inward listing, and allocate the proceeds into a ZAR operational current account after conversion. For a TikTok Shop retail entity, the capitalisation should clearly state 'inward capital investment for working capital' to avoid misclassification as a loan or trade settlement, which would trigger a different compliance path.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlements should be routed through SWIFT MT103/MT102 payment instructions in ZAR, USD, EUR, or CNY to the beneficiary bank, with a Commercial Letter of Credit or Documentary Collection for high-value bulk inventory purchases requiring title verification. Domestic disbursements, including logistics, warehousing, and local TikTok platform settlement, should use the South African national payment system (Sa-TS / STR) through bank EFT. All outward foreign payments require SARS import documentation (Bill of Entry) and authorised-dealer approval; same-day ZAR clearing is facilitated through BankservAfrica, while SWIFT-based cross-border payments settle within one to three business days depending on intermediary bank configuration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) with authorised dealers, deliverable in ZAR, for committed trade obligations up to 12 months
Cross-currency swaps with licensed banks for balance-sheet ZAR/USD liability hedging
Purchased Foreign Exchange Options from an authorised dealer; speculative short option positions are not permitted for Tier 1 e-commerce operators
Non-deliverable forwards are allowed only for offshore counterparties and solely as correlation hedging against verifiable underlying trade flows, never as a standalone speculative instrument

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) including Beneficial Ownership (BO) declaration and declared turnover band
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days of the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company flagged non-compliant; late-filing penalty per compliance notice; two consecutive years of non-filing trigger administrative strike-off under s.82(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; directors may be held personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) approved, retained and tabled to shareholders; no CIPC filing required for a private (Pty) Ltd
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (retention obligation only, unless PIS or ministerial directive requires filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared and approved within 6 months of financial year-end; retained for 7 years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directoral offence under s.30 and s.34 of the Companies Act; compliance notice or administrative penalty; directors subject to personal liability for defective financial reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return (ITR14) for the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of financial year-end, or the earlier date stated in the SARS return notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty under s.210 Tax Administration Act (up to 10% of assessed tax); 10% monthly interest; understatement penalties of 20% to 125%.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: First provisional tax estimate and payment (IRP6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the start of the year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of 10% (low-risk) or 15% (standard) of unpaid provisional tax, plus 10% monthly interest; estimate penalty under paragraph 20 of the Fourth Schedule to the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Second provisional tax estimate and payment (IRP6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last business day of the final month of the year of assessment (financial year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of 20% of unpaid provisional tax where taxable income exceeds ZAR 20,000; 10% monthly interest; 20% estimate-accuracy penalty where provisional payment is below 90% of assessed liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Third provisional tax payment (voluntary top-up; IRP6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Optional; interest and late-payment penalties apply to the residual balance upon final assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Public Interest Score (PIS) computation and engagement of auditor or independent reviewer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors (internal; regulatory records reviewed by CIPC on inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, during AFS preparation and before the 6-month approval deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain the legally required assurance level makes the AFS non-compliant; director liability for defective reporting under s.29 and administrative penalties under s.214 of the Companies Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit for (i) public or state-owned companies, and (ii) any company with a Public Interest Score (PIS) of at least 500. A PIS of 350-499 requires an audit unless shareholders elect an independent review by resolution; a PIS of 100-349 requires an independent review where the AFS are internally compiled; a PIS below 100 exempts a private retail company from both audit and review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (adopted by the Financial Reporting Standards Council) for ordinary (Pty) Ltd entities; full IFRS applies to companies with a PIS of 350 or more that must be audited, and to any public or state-owned company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 2022, a (Pty) Ltd must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register identifying every individual with 5% or more beneficial interest; the BO declaration is confirmed annually with the CIPC Annual Return on the incorporation anniversary, and any transfer of beneficial ownership must be updated in the register and filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder and director resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 95-390 per year (ZAR 1,500-6,500) for a registered office and company secretarial retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable where PIS is below 100; if an audit is triggered: 2,000-6,000 (ZAR 35,000-105,000); independent review: 600-1,500 (ZAR 10,000-25,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Preferential deductions include: Section 12B 100% first-year deduction for renewable-energy assets; Section 12I industrial investment allowance; Section 11D R&D deduction; Section 12C/12CA capital allowances on movable assets; Special Economic Zone (SEZ) trading income taxed at 15% for approved SEZ operators; and ordinary s11(a) deductions for operating expenses, platform fees, and advertising costs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward, provided the company continues the same trade and ownership/trade continuity tests are met)
